aiOverview.text:
Continual and incremental learning
enables smart meters—reading data every few seconds or minutes—to identify and adapt to new residential appliances over time without forgetting previously learned devices
[MDPI]
in low-frequency non-intrusive load monitoring (NILM)


Core Challenges in Low-Frequency NILM
- Catastrophic Forgetting: When a machine learning model learns a newly introduced appliance class, its accuracy on older, previously recognized appliances tends to degrade severely.
- Static Label Spaces: Traditional supervised NILM models rely on fixed output categories, making them blind to new or custom appliances added by homeowners.
- Data Scarcity & High Sampling Gaps: Low-frequency data (seconds to minutes) lacks rich transient waveforms (like high-frequency current harmonics), forcing models to rely mostly on steady-state active power changes.


Emerging Solutions and Architectures
- Analytic and Class-Incremental Methods: Techniques like Nearest Class Mean Forests (NCM-Forest) use dynamic centroid-based partitions and partial subtree retraining to incorporate new appliance signatures seamlessly.
- Dual-Branch and Lightweight Models: Systems employ depthwise separable convolutions for simultaneous load identification and novelty detection (spotting when an unknown appliance turns on).
- Collaborative and Distributed Frameworks: Confidence-based continual learning frameworks allow edge devices or smart meters to update local sub-models rapidly via one-time fine-tuning while resolving cross-client knowledge conflicts.
